components.css: .ds-btn-primary { height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--primary, oklch(0.47 0.158 267.4)); color: var(--primary-foreground, #fff); font: 500 14px/20px 'Figtree Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, oklch(0.47 0.158 267.4)) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.47 0.158 267.4)) 30%, transparent); }

narrative.overview: Ping is where Spark's staff spend their working day clearing Pings and following Threads, so the room has to stay calm for eight hours. A steady ink navy frame (top bar and sidebar) holds a bright work surface: a white panel inset on the chrome on a laptop, over a cool, navy-tinted grey feed. Nothing in the frame competes for attention. Colour appears only where something needs a person: a pink Ping count, a green Saved marker, an indigo action.
keyCharacteristics: Ink navy chrome around a bright, inset work surface.
Colour is a signal, never decoration: indigo acts, pink needs you, green is Saved, red is danger.
Compact density with soft, friendly shapes.
Flat surfaces separated by tone; shadows only on things that float.
Every text pair meets WCAG AA, in both themes.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Pink, green, indigo and red each mean one thing. Never use Ping Pink for decoration, a brand moment or an error, and never use a signal colour as a large fill.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Greys lean toward the navy hue (about 260 in OKLCH, low chroma). Don't introduce a pure grey or a warm stone.

rules.name: The Six Sizes Rule
rules.body: Use only the six steps (text-xs, text-small, text-sm, text-base, text-lg, text-xl). The one exception is the Ping wordmark on the sign-in page.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: On a phone, inputs and textareas render at 16px so iOS doesn't zoom on focus. They drop to 14px from the md breakpoint.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Thread rows, the Channel bar and the inset panel have no shadow. Use a Hairline border or a tone step instead.

dos: Do build from apps/web/src/components/ui and the tokens in apps/web/src/index.css. Add a missing piece with pnpm dlx shadcn@4.23.0 add <name> from apps/web, then adapt it to these rules.
Do use semantic utilities (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, bg-ping, text-saved, bg-sidebar), never raw colours like bg-blue-500.
Do check every new text pair for 4.5:1 contrast in both themes, and check new screens at laptop and phone width.
Do compose: compound components and explicit variants, children over render props (.claude/skills/vercel-composition-patterns).
Do use lucide-react icons at 16px, decorative (aria-hidden), with the meaning in text or an accessible name.
donts: Don't add per-feature CSS files or @apply in components. index.css holds tokens and base styles only.
Don't use Ping Pink, Saved Green or Alarm Red for anything but their one meaning (The Signal Rule).
Don't add shadows to in-flow surfaces like Thread rows or the Channel bar (The Flat-By-Default Rule).
Don't add a boolean prop that switches a component's mode. Make an explicit variant or a separate component.
Don't load fonts, icons or scripts from a CDN: the CSP allows only this origin, and no Staff member's data goes to a third party.
Don't use gradients, glows, blur or purple-to-pink decoration.
